question: What should the first OpenClaw-owned skill permission manifest contract include, and how should declared permissions relate to install consent, audit/trust scoring, signing, attestation, ClawHub verification, and runtime enforcement?
rationale: This defines a public ecosystem security boundary; automation cannot safely choose schema placement, trust roots, consent semantics, or enforcement timing from source inspection alone.

options.title: Consolidate Security Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor and use the related RFCs, plugins, forks, and partial PRs as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

options.title: Land Audit-Only Metadata First
options.body: Accept a narrow optional declaration surface that is explicitly inspect-only, then track consent, signing, attestation, and enforcement in later phases.

options.title: Keep Trust Scoring External
options.body: Let ClawHub or governance plugins own declarations and trust scoring unless a concrete missing core/plugin API is identified.

recommendation.title: Consolidate Security Design First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor and use the related RFCs, plugins, forks, and partial PRs as input before accepting a public manifest contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the skills CLI/native install history and the latest visible product/security review of this issue.
